Prevention: Carefully choose sites for crucifer seedbeds that do not have a history of club root.
If there is any doubt about soil contamination, then increase to pH 7 of the seedbed areas.
If a field is known to be infested, the soil pH should be adjusted to pH 6.8 to 7 with ground limestone (CaCO3).
Always thoroughly clean farm equipment after working in a field suspected of having the club root fungus.
Plant resistant variety if available, e.g.
Crop rotation with a non-crucifer crop like corn or rice
Monitoring: Monitor fields regularly – at weekly intervals
Look for poor crop growth or stunted plants; confirm disease by uprooting affected plants to confirm the presence of root deformation.
Direct Control: Remove all infected plant roots and destroy by burning.
Restrictions: No known chemical control that is effective as it is a soil born disease.
